title: Why Do You Weigh Less at Earth's Equator?
description:
What If Earth Stopped Spinning?
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6bbbvfCx6zY

Because the ground at the equator swings round so fast, you weigh about half of one percent less there than at the poles, and the whole planet bulges.

Sources: NGA Technical Report TR8350.2 (WGS 84), Table 3.4, equatorial gravity 9.7803 m/s² vs polar gravity 9.8322 m/s² (about 0.53% less) · NASA GSFC Earth Fact Sheet (Williams), equatorial radius 6,378.1 km vs polar radius 6,356.8 km (about 43 km wider across the equator). https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html

Pictures: NASA (ISS, DSCOVR/EPIC, GSFC Blue Marble), ESA/NASA (Alexander Gerst ISS time-lapse), ESO (La Silla Observatory time-lapse, CC BY 4.0), NOAA (GOES-16 satellite imagery), and Foucault pendulum footage, alongside AI-assisted voice and editing. Facts: every number is checked against the sources listed above.
Image credits: NASA; ESA/NASA; ESO; NOAA.
